_comment: Example broker policy. Each target names a staging root, a production root, allowed file patterns, a sandbox health check and a production health check. apply_enabled=true lets the broker apply and, if the production check fails, roll back. min_checkpoint_state is the autonomy level a request needs before it is applied; below it the request is escalated to the operator.

a2a-gateway._comment: B4 (2026-09-26): apply enabled, but min_checkpoint_state stays fully_autonomous -- until  climbs, every gateway request escalates to the operator (P_CHECKPOINT_STATE) and nothing is applied.

broker-dummy._comment: Throwaway B3 test target. The prod check requires the body to contain 'HEALTH_OK' so a deliberately bad change passes the sandbox but fails production, exercising the automatic rollback. (First live run used the marker 'OK', which 'BROKEN' contains -- lesson: health markers must be distinctive.)

git._comment: G2 (2026-10-09): apply/rollback enabled for the throwaway dummy ONLY, same B3 pattern applied to schema_version "2". Distinct units/ports from the v1 dummy above so the two never collide. production_root must already be a baseline-committed git repo (the operator does this by hand, once, outside the broker) before this is ever relied on.
